Doxorubicin is indicated for the treatment of metastatic soft tissue sarcoma (label section 1.2, among other cancers).

blocking_factors: No baseline echocardiogram or LVEF on file before an anthracycline
ECOG 1 is an intake assumption, not clinician-documented
No laboratory values of any kind were supplied at intake

Myelosuppression that must be read against altitude-shifted baseline blood counts at 8,500 ft
Febrile neutropenia 9% as a single agent in LMS-04, well below the combination's 28%

rationale: Single-agent doxorubicin holds the strongest guideline position in this disease: BSG 2025 grades it I,A as standard first-line treatment, and metastatic soft tissue sarcoma is on the US label. It occupies the same first-line slot as the planned doxorubicin plus trabectedin combination, which beat it on PFS and OS in LMS-04 but remains off-label at this line and is ranked on the Experimental table. Whichever is chosen, the missing baseline echocardiogram is the true gate on cycle 1.
notes: ESMO's operative soft tissue sarcoma guideline is the 2021 edition (pmid:34303806) and predates LMS-04; it was not quotable in full this session, so the guideline anchor here is BSG 2025 plus the label. NCCN carriage is behind a login wall and no NCCN category is quoted anywhere in this table.

option_label: Tumour NGS with germline TP53 testing before genotoxic chemotherapy

endorsements.designation: ESMO Precision Medicine Working Group recommendation, 2024 update
endorsements.indication_text: Tumour NGS recommendations expanded to encompass rare tumours including sarcoma, and tumour NGS is recommended to detect tumour-agnostic alterations in metastatic cancers where access to matched therapies is available.

Li-Fraumeni and heritable TP53-related cancer syndromes: soft-tissue sarcoma sits in the tumour spectrum, and radiotherapy and conventional genotoxic chemotherapy contribute to subsequent primary tumours in carriers, so germline status is best established before such therapy.

eligibility_rationale: The 2024 resection block exists and no result is pending; only the consent conversation and a records and block-release request stand between her and the panel.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: This is the same panel, consent conversation and block-allocation question the Experimental table carries at rank 1, and it is what opens or closes the pembrolizumab and TRK rows below. One requisition set serves both tables.

rationale: Tumour NGS in sarcoma moved from clinician preference to guideline-backed workup in the ESMO 2024 precision-medicine update, and ERN GENTURIS puts the germline TP53 answer before genotoxic chemotherapy because uLMS sits in the Li-Fraumeni spectrum. On this table the panel is the key that opens or closes both tumour-agnostic approval doors. The germline draw is a consent conversation with consequences for her relatives, and whether she wants that information has not been asked.

option_label: Baseline echocardiogram, cardiac surveillance and cumulative anthracycline planning

endorsements.indication_text: Prevention and monitoring of cardiac dysfunction in adults receiving potentially cardiotoxic therapy, including anthracyclines: discuss risk before beginning therapy, with prevention and screening strategies during treatment for higher-risk patients.

endorsements.designation: 2022 ESC cardio-oncology guideline (developed with EHA, ESTRO and IC-OS)
endorsements.indication_text: Baseline cardiovascular risk assessment including echocardiography before anthracycline chemotherapy, with surveillance during and after treatment.

eligibility_rationale: Nothing in the profile blocks an echocardiogram; the problem is that it has not been done and induction is imminent.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The echocardiogram in this row is the same one the Experimental table's rank-1 workup names as a true gate on cycle 1 of the ranked induction regimen; a failed screen moves the first-line conversation to this table's gemcitabine plus docetaxel row.

rationale: A baseline echocardiogram before an anthracycline is standard care under both the ASCO 2017 and ESC 2022 cardio-oncology guidelines, and it was an eligibility criterion of the trial her planned regimen comes from; none exists in her chart. At her age the cumulative doxorubicin dose is a lifetime ledger, so the dose-cap and dexrazoxane conversation belongs before cycle 1, noting honestly that the dexrazoxane label population (metastatic breast cancer after 300 mg/m2 of doxorubicin) is not hers. A pathogenic germline TP53 result would re-open the whole genotoxic plan.

option_label: Primary G-CSF prophylaxis through induction chemotherapy

endorsements.indication_text: Prophylactic use of colony-stimulating factors is warranted when the risk of febrile neutropenia is approximately 20% or higher and no equally effective and safe regimen that does not require CSFs is available.

eligibility_rationale: No contraindication in the profile; the planned combination regimen's 28% febrile neutropenia rate puts her above the ASCO prophylaxis threshold from cycle 1.

evidence.population: first-line metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma
evidence.effect_size: grade 3-4 neutropenia 80% and febrile neutropenia 28% in the doxorubicin plus trabectedin arm, vs 13% and 9% with doxorubicin alone

toxicity_highlights: Bone pain is the common G-CSF toxicity; the trade is against a 28% febrile neutropenia rate

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Belongs in the cycle 1 orders of the ranked induction regimen. If single-agent doxorubicin is chosen instead, its 9% febrile neutropenia rate sits below the ASCO threshold, so the G-CSF call follows the regimen choice.

rationale: The planned induction produced febrile neutropenia in 28% of trial patients, above the roughly 20% threshold at which ASCO recommends primary G-CSF prophylaxis, so growth-factor support belongs in the cycle 1 orders rather than being discovered at cycle 2. Neutropenic-fever counselling also needs the altitude context: baseline counts and oximetry at 8,500 ft shift the reference ranges the fever thresholds are read against.

option_label: Fertility and ovarian-function counselling before gonadotoxic chemotherapy

endorsements.indication_text: Providers should initiate the discussion of possible infertility with patients treated during their reproductive years as early as possible before treatment starts; oocyte cryopreservation is standard practice; evidence for GnRH-agonist ovarian suppression is conflicting and it should not replace proven methods.

eligibility_rationale: She is in her thirties with presumably retained ovaries after a hysterectomy done for a presumed fibroid; the profile records no counselling and no reproductive-endocrinology referral.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Any oocyte retrieval or suppression decision has to land before the ranked induction begins. This names the timing pressure; it is not an argument to delay treatment, and the window is days rather than weeks.

rationale: She is 30-39 and days from chemotherapy that can end ovarian function, and the record shows no one has raised it; hysterectomy settled childbearing anatomy but not oocytes, hormones or menopause timing. ASCO places this discussion before therapy starts, as early as possible, because the widest option set exists only before cycle 1. What ovarian function and the hormonal aftermath mean to her is one of the four questions the advocate flagged as never asked.

endorsements.indication_text: First-line alternative to doxorubicin across sarcoma subtypes: GeDDiS showed the regimen non-inferior to doxorubicin but more toxic; activity demonstrated in leiomyosarcoma and undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma.

eligibility_rationale: Chemotherapy-naive, so the slot is open; docetaxel needs a hepatic panel that does not exist yet, and pneumonitis surveillance needs the pulmonary baseline and altitude-adjusted oximetry the rank-1 workup orders.
blocking_factors: No hepatic panel on file (docetaxel dosing)
No pulmonary function tests or oximetry baseline at her 8,500 ft residence for pneumonitis surveillance
ECOG 1 is an intake assumption, not clinician-documented

evidence.design: randomized phase 3, first line, all STS subtypes
evidence.population: previously untreated advanced or metastatic STS; 46% leiomyosarcoma, 28% of the trial uterine LMS
evidence.primary_endpoint: proportion alive and progression-free at 24 weeks
evidence.effect_size: 46.4% vs 46.3% alive and progression-free at 24 weeks; PFS HR 1.28 (95% CI 0.99-1.65) not favouring gemcitabine plus docetaxel; more toxic than doxorubicin

evidence.population: chemotherapy-naive metastatic uterine leiomyosarcoma
evidence.effect_size: ORR 35.8% (95% CI 23.5-49.6); median PFS 4.4 months

toxicity_highlights: Both drugs carry pneumonitis risk, which would be hard to read against bilateral infiltrative lung disease and altitude-shifted oximetry
Docetaxel fluid retention, neuropathy and myelosuppression; GeDDiS logged more toxicity than doxorubicin

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Holds the fallback slot for the same first-line window the ranked LMS-04 regimen occupies: a failed echocardiogram or pulmonary screen moves the first-line conversation here without touching the rest of the ranking.

rationale: The main first-line alternative when an anthracycline is unwise: BSG 2025 carries it at II,B as non-inferior to doxorubicin though more toxic, and it has dedicated first-line uLMS data (ORR 35.8% in GOG 087L). The PI's synthesis names it the fallback if the cardiac or pulmonary baseline disqualifies doxorubicin, and that is exactly where it sits on this table. Its pneumonitis liability deserves naming in advance against her lungs and her altitude.
notes: The original MSKCC phase 2 (pmid:12065559) reported ORR 53% in a mixed-line, 85% uterine LMS cohort and anchors the regimen's LMS reputation.

endorsements.indication_text: Adults with advanced soft tissue sarcoma who have received prior chemotherapy; efficacy not demonstrated in adipocytic STS or GIST.
Metastatic STS (not liposarcoma) after prior chemotherapy, on a 3-month progression-free survival improvement over placebo.

eligibility_rationale: Label and trial evidence both require prior chemotherapy, and she is systemic-therapy naive until induction runs; the population match becomes exact at first progression.
blocking_factors: Label requires prior chemotherapy; she has had no systemic therapy yet

evidence.population: metastatic non-adipocytic STS after standard chemotherapy, anthracycline required
evidence.effect_size: median PFS 4.6 vs 1.6 months, HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.24-0.40); overall survival not significantly improved

evidence.design: retrospective pooling of two prospective EORTC trials
evidence.population: advanced uterine sarcoma, 88.6% uLMS, heavily pretreated
evidence.effect_size: ORR 11% (95% CI 3.8-24.6); median PFS 3.0 months

toxicity_highlights: Hypertension and transaminitis with scheduled liver-function monitoring
Pneumothorax has been reported in sarcoma patients with lung metastases
VEGFR-class wound-healing impairment would interact with any later lung-directed surgery

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: At first progression this approved anchor and the ranked experimental doors ask for the same treatment slot; an on-label option a payer recognises exists at that line whichever way the team goes. Its wound-healing liability would also matter if metastasectomy ever became real.

rationale: The on-label second-line anchor: approved for advanced STS after prior chemotherapy on PALETTE's PFS effect (HR 0.31), carried by BSG 2025 at II,B. Its uterine-LMS-specific evidence is thinner than the label reads: a retrospective pooling of 44 heavily pretreated uterine sarcoma patients with ORR 11% and median PFS 3.0 months. It becomes live at first progression, where it shares the slot with the HRD-conditional PARP branch and the phase 1 doors the Experimental table ranks.

option_label: Early specialist palliative care alongside active treatment

endorsements.indication_text: Patients with advanced solid tumours should be referred to specialised interdisciplinary palliative care teams beginning early in the disease course, alongside active treatment of their cancer.
Supportive and palliative care should always be considered in advanced disease, with early referral to specialist palliative care services.

eligibility_rationale: Metastatic disease with cough and dyspnea; nothing blocks a referral, and none is recorded.

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Runs alongside induction and every later branch; it neither delays nor competes with any ranked option.

rationale: Concurrent specialist palliative care from early in metastatic disease is an ASCO recommendation rather than a late-stage handoff, and BSG 2025 says the same for advanced sarcoma. In this case it also hosts the conversation nobody has had: goals of care were never discussed at intake and every preference on file is an assumed default. A symptom-control referral is a natural place for the four unasked questions to finally get asked.

endorsements.indication_text: First-line advanced STS: the combination has not been shown to improve survival over single-agent doxorubicin; response rates and PFS are higher at greater toxicity, and it may be considered in individual patients where a response would improve symptoms.

eligibility_rationale: Her age band fits the EORTC 62012 population (18-60, PS 0-1), but the missing baselines bite harder here: ifosfamide needs the renal panel that does not exist, on top of the absent echocardiogram.
blocking_factors: No renal panel on file (ifosfamide nephrotoxicity)
No baseline echocardiogram before an anthracycline
ECOG 1 is an intake assumption, not clinician-documented

evidence.population: first-line advanced or metastatic high-grade STS, age 18-60, PS 0-1
evidence.effect_size: median OS 14.3 vs 12.8 months, HR 0.83 (95.5% CI 0.67-1.03, p=0.076); higher ORR and PFS with substantially more toxicity

toxicity_highlights: Febrile neutropenia 46% vs 13% with doxorubicin alone in EORTC 62012
Ifosfamide encephalopathy and nephrotoxicity
Shares the cumulative anthracycline ledger with every other doxorubicin-containing option

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: A third occupant of the single chemotherapy-naive first-line slot the ranked LMS-04 regimen is planned to spend; listing it does not reopen the choice, it maps the slot.

rationale: Carried at II,B for the situation where tumour shrinkage itself is the goal, since the combination buys response rate and PFS but not survival (EORTC 62012 OS HR 0.83 with the upper bound crossing 1). Two case-specific facts keep it at a completeness listing: leiomyosarcoma is among the less ifosfamide-sensitive histologies, and her symptomatic lung disease already has a response-seeking plan in the ranked induction.

endorsements.indication_text: Adults with unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma who received a prior anthracycline-containing regimen.

endorsements.designation: British Sarcoma Group (BSG): licensed second-line agent
endorsements.indication_text: Licensed as second-line treatment for all soft tissue sarcomas, with activity in leiomyosarcoma and liposarcoma; NICE approves continuation until disease progression.

eligibility_rationale: The label requires a prior anthracycline she has not yet had; more importantly, the planned first line already contains trabectedin through maintenance, so at progression the drug would usually count as spent.
blocking_factors: Label requires a prior anthracycline-containing regimen; she is systemic-therapy naive
The planned LMS-04 first line delivers trabectedin to progression through its maintenance phase, which would close this on-label second-line use

evidence.effect_size: median PFS 4.2 vs 1.5 months, HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.44-0.70); grade 3+ ALT elevation 25%, treatment-related deaths 2.1%

evidence.effect_size: PFS HR 0.57, mirroring the parent trial

Rhabdomyolysis 1.2% and treatment-related mortality 2.1% in the registration trial

rationale: On label this is the classic second-line drug for uLMS after an anthracycline, with a randomized PFS advantage over dacarbazine (HR 0.55) that held in the uterine subset. Her case bends the sequence: the planned first line already delivers trabectedin to progression through its maintenance phase, which would spend this slot before she reaches it. If the first line ends up being doxorubicin alone instead, this row returns to the table intact.

endorsements.indication_text: Gemcitabine plus dacarbazine as an alternative later-line regimen in advanced STS, generally well tolerated.

eligibility_rationale: No case-specific block once earlier lines are spent; no organ-function labs exist yet, as everywhere in this record.

evidence.population: previously treated advanced soft tissue sarcoma
evidence.effect_size: median PFS 4.2 vs 2.0 months (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.86); median OS 16.8 vs 8.2 months (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.36-0.90)

toxicity_highlights: Generally well tolerated; granulocytopenia the main serious event, febrile neutropenia uncommon
Gemcitabine pneumonitis risk reads poorly against her infiltrative lung disease

The order in which this row is reached matters more than usual.

rationale: A tolerable later-line option with a randomized signal: gemcitabine plus dacarbazine beat dacarbazine alone on PFS and OS in previously treated STS, and BSG 2025 carries it at II,B. Its main case-specific weight is a foreclosure: dacarbazine exposure would exclude her from the randomized trial behind the Experimental table's PARP branch, so sequencing, not efficacy, is what this row is really about.

endorsements.indication_text: Selected patients with thoracic metastases: long-term survivors are reported (20-40% of patients undergoing lung surgery) although prospective data are few and the survival benefit remains unproven.

eligibility_rationale: Bilateral infiltrative, possibly inflammatory pulmonary disease is the anatomy the surgical series screened out, and the staging record is incomplete: the 2024 operative report has not been retrieved.
blocking_factors: Bilateral infiltrative disease pattern; the resection series selected patients with countable, resectable lesions
Morcellation status of the 2024 resection unknown; if morcellation occurred, peritoneal restaging precedes any consolidation planning (abdominopelvic dissemination 44% vs 12.9% in the cited series)
No pulmonary function tests or oximetry baseline, read against an 8,500 ft residence

evidence.population: resectable lung metastases; sarcoma 42% of the registry
evidence.effect_size: 5-year OS 36% after complete resection; median OS 35 vs 15 months for complete vs incomplete resection

evidence.population: sarcoma pulmonary metastasectomy; LMS subset 31 patients
evidence.effect_size: median OS 70 months in the LMS subset vs 24 months non-LMS (p=0.049)

toxicity_highlights: Thoracotomy morbidity and permanently lost pulmonary reserve, priced differently for someone living at 8,500 ft

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Only becomes assessable if the ranked induction converts bilateral infiltrative disease into a resectable pattern, and after the rank-1 workup retrieves the 2024 operative report; the morcellation answer decides whether peritoneal restaging comes first.

rationale: Guideline-carried for selected patients, and the long-term survivors in the registries are real, but every series is retrospective and operability-selected, and bilateral infiltrative disease is exactly what they screened out. The honest framing is the PI's: a question to re-ask if induction converts the anatomy, not a survival number to quote today. Two records gate it before anatomy even matters: the 2024 operative report and a measured pulmonary baseline at her altitude.

option_label: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to pulmonary metastases

endorsements.designation: British Sarcoma Group (BSG): named option, evidence limited
endorsements.indication_text: Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy has become another potential option for lung metastases from STS, with evidence still limited.

eligibility_rationale: The SBRT series treated small numbers of countable lesions with a controlled primary; bilateral diffuse infiltrative disease is not currently a stereotactic target, and no pulmonary baseline exists.
blocking_factors: Bilateral diffuse infiltrative disease is not an oligometastatic SBRT target; the cited series treated up to a few discrete lesions
No pulmonary function baseline at 8,500 ft; lost lung volume carries a higher price at altitude
Consolidation intent shares the unresolved 2024 morcellation and staging question with the surgical row

evidence.population: oligometastatic sarcoma lung metastases, 56 lesions
evidence.effect_size: local control 90% (95% CI 84-96) at 24 months, alongside overall survival 46% at 24 months in the same patients

evidence.population: STS lung metastases unsuitable for resection, up to 4 lesions, controlled primary
evidence.effect_size: actuarial 5-year local control 96%

toxicity_highlights: Radiation pneumonitis would be difficult to separate from disease progression and altitude physiology in these lungs

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Like the surgical row, this is a consolidation question that only opens if the ranked induction converts the anatomy; the same operative-report and staging gates apply.

rationale: The non-surgical consolidation route, named by BSG 2025 as a potential option with limited evidence. The series are retrospective and eligibility-selected, and their headline numbers measure different things: the same 44-patient cohort shows 90% local control at 24 months and 46% survival at 24 months, so ablating visible lesions and changing the disease course are separate claims. Like metastasectomy, this is a question to re-ask if induction converts bilateral infiltrative disease into countable targets.

endorsements.indication_text: Unresectable or metastatic liposarcoma after a prior anthracycline-containing regimen; leiomyosarcoma is not in the US label.

endorsements.designation: British Sarcoma Group (BSG): noted, liposarcoma authorisation
endorsements.indication_text: Marketing authorisation for unresectable liposarcoma; data in other sarcoma types limited; not currently funded in England.

eligibility_rationale: Medically she could receive it after an anthracycline, but the label covers liposarcoma, so any use in her histology is off-label and rests on a null subgroup.
blocking_factors: Requires a prior anthracycline-containing regimen; not yet given
US label excludes leiomyosarcoma, so use in her histology is off-label

evidence.population: advanced liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after 2 or more prior regimens including an anthracycline
evidence.effect_size: median OS 13.5 vs 11.5 months, HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.62-0.95), driven by the liposarcoma stratum

evidence.population: advanced leiomyosarcoma, 42% uterine
evidence.effect_size: OS HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.71-1.20, p=0.57); median PFS 2.2 vs 2.6 months, numerically worse than dacarbazine

toxicity_highlights: Neutropenia and neuropathy, the familiar microtubule-inhibitor profile

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: By third line the approved shelf in LMS is thin, which is the backdrop against which the ranked phase 1 doors were surfaced; this row shares that slot without arguing against them.

rationale: Carried for completeness and honesty rather than promise: the OS benefit that won eribulin its approval came from the liposarcoma stratum, the US label is liposarcoma-only, and the leiomyosarcoma subgroup is null (OS HR 0.93 with PFS numerically worse than dacarbazine). For her histology this is a drug the later-line conversation will mention and the data do not support well. That thin later-line shelf is itself a finding of this screen.

endorsements.indication_text: Adult and pediatric patients with unresectable or metastatic MSI-H or dMMR solid tumours, as determined by an FDA-authorized test, that have progressed following prior treatment and who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options.
endorsements.version_or_date: FDA accelerated approval 2017-05; DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-12

endorsements.indication_text: Adult and pediatric patients with unresectable or metastatic TMB-high (10 or more mutations per megabase) solid tumours, as determined by an FDA-authorized test, that have progressed following prior treatment and who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options.
endorsements.version_or_date: FDA accelerated approval 2020-06; DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-12

eligibility_rationale: Both gating biomarkers are untested rather than negative, and the label also requires progression on prior therapy, a line she has not yet reached. The missing facts are the MSI/MMR and TMB results the ordered NGS panel will return.

biomarker_requirement.threshold: MSI-H or dMMR by an FDA-authorized test; or TMB >= 10 mut/Mb

evidence.primary_endpoint: objective response rate by central review
evidence.effect_size: ORR 34.3% (95% CI 28.3-40.8); median PFS 4.1 months

evidence.population: previously treated advanced solid tumours with evaluable TMB
evidence.effect_size: ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39) in TMB >= 10 mut/Mb vs 6% (95% CI 5-8) below

toxicity_highlights: Immune-related pneumonitis would be hard to read against bilateral infiltrative lung disease and altitude-shifted oximetry

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: The gate closes on the same one-pass NGS panel the Experimental rank-1 workup orders; nothing extra is spent. A positive would move this row to on-label care at progression.

rationale: Two tumour-agnostic approval doors that testing would open: pembrolizumab is approved for MSI-H/dMMR and for TMB-H solid tumours after progression on prior therapy. Both markers are currently untested rather than negative, both are rare in uLMS, and both close cheaply on the NGS panel already in the rank-1 workup. Until a result returns, the population match is unknowable, which is why this row sits behind a workup gate rather than in the consider-now group.
notes: The TMB half of this gate is the biomarker-survey row tmb-high-not-measured; the MSI/MMR half is linked above. Checkpoint activity in unselected LMS has historically been modest, so the doors matter only if a marker returns positive.

option_label: TRK inhibitor (larotrectinib or entrectinib), tumour-agnostic if NTRK fusion-positive

endorsements.indication_text: Adult and pediatric patients with solid tumours that have an NTRK gene fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation, are metastatic or where resection would cause severe morbidity, and have no satisfactory alternative treatments or have progressed following treatment.
endorsements.version_or_date: FDA accelerated approval 2018-11; Vitrakvi label revised 4/2025, DailyMed accessed 2026-08-12

eligibility_rationale: NTRK fusion status has never been tested; the profile is silent on the single fact that gates the entire option.

biomarker_requirement.threshold: NTRK1/2/3 fusion without a known acquired resistance mutation, ideally by RNA-inclusive fusion calling

evidence.design: pooled analysis of three phase 1/2 trials
evidence.population: TRK fusion-positive solid tumours across histologies

toxicity_highlights: Dizziness, fatigue and weight gain; a benign profile relative to the cytotoxic rows

relationship_to_targeted_options.note: Priced by the same rank-1 requisition; the workup already specifies RNA-inclusive fusion calling because a DNA-only panel could return a false negative that reads as a closed question.

rationale: The second tumour-agnostic door: TRK inhibitors carry a pooled ORR of 79% in NTRK fusion-positive tumours, but the fusion is vanishingly rare in uLMS and hers is untested rather than negative. The requisition detail decides the answer's quality, since several common panels are DNA-only and the rank-1 workup already specifies RNA-inclusive fusion calling. A positive would be on-label care; the prior is low.

endorsements.designation: British Sarcoma Group (BSG): option limited to receptor-expressing tumours
endorsements.indication_text: Endocrine therapy in uterine sarcoma is reserved for hormone-receptor-expressing, typically more indolent tumours; the supporting phase 2 required ER and/or PR expression.

eligibility_rationale: ER <1% and PR <1% by IHC, recorded as a confirmed decision-relevant negative; the trial that supports letrozole in uLMS required receptor expression and saw durable benefit only above 90% staining.
blocking_factors: ER <1% and PR <1% by IHC, a confirmed decision-relevant negative
Specimen provenance of the ER/PR stain (2024 primary vs 2026 lung core) is unverified; the foreclosure holds only as firmly as that check

evidence.population: unresectable uLMS expressing ER and/or PR
evidence.effect_size: 12-week PFS 50% (90% CI 30-67); durable benefit confined to tumours staining above 90%

rationale: Listed so its absence is explained rather than wondered about: endocrine therapy in uLMS belongs to receptor-expressing tumours, and hers stained under 1% for both ER and PR, which closes this door. The one residual thread is provenance: if the stain came off the 2024 block rather than current disease, the restain in the rank-1 workup could in principle reopen the question, though a true conversion is unlikely.
notes: The ER/PR provenance check lives in the Experimental table's rank-1 workup; this row simply inherits its outcome.
